title: CUB architecture-matched zero-keypoint control
purpose: Resolve the architecture confound in the sparse-keypoint premise by comparing Random-K1 against an otherwise identical PrPool K0 arm.

dependency.observed_confound: GLOBAL uses global average pooling while RANDOM_K1 uses a 16-map PrPool classifier; their difference cannot be attributed only to keypoint supervision.

data.episodes: reuse the three frozen PAT-D-260728-009 official-train episodes

arm.PRPOOL_K0: Identical PrPool architecture, optimizer, complement regularizer, augmentation, fold seeds, and nine-epoch budget as RANDOM_K1, but no image receives keypoint loss.

references.GLOBAL: reported only for context; not the causal keypoint baseline

primary_endpoints: paired Random-K1 minus PrPool-K0 OOF balanced-accuracy gain per episode
paired Full-Oracle minus PrPool-K0 OOF balanced-accuracy gain per episode
Random-K1 class negative-transfer rate versus PrPool-K0

go_no_go.sparse_keypoint_value_isolated_if: Mean Random-K1 minus PrPool-K0 gain is at least 1.0 pp and at least two of three episode gains are at least 0.5 pp.
go_no_go.full_keypoint_value_isolated_if: Mean Full-Oracle minus PrPool-K0 gain is at least 2.0 pp and at least two of three episode gains are at least 1.0 pp.
go_no_go.overall_go: Both isolated-value gates pass and official test access remains zero.
go_no_go.on_go: Sparse keypoint value is real after architecture matching; formulate class-level budget allocation or worst-class-risk work.
go_no_go.on_no_go: Retract the causal sparse-keypoint value interpretation, retain only the PrPool architecture result, and stop the CUB sparse-keypoint direction.
